title: Implement performance-first regex backend matrix with max supported fat-runtime coverage
agent_instructions: Treat this JSON as the authoritative task specification.
Inspect the current repository state before editing anything.
Keep changes tightly scoped to backend selection, dependency configuration, runtime validation, CI, and documentation.
Do not ask follow-up questions. Make the best defensible implementation and clearly document any blockers.

windows-arm64.note: Do not enable Vectorscan yet. Preserve clean extension points for the next task.

core_objectives: Implement deterministic build-time backend selection by OS and architecture.
Use Hyperscan on all x86_64 targets in the target matrix.
Use Vectorscan on Linux arm64 and macOS arm64.
Keep Windows arm64 on Qt fallback only for now.
Maximize fat-runtime use where the selected backend and target platform support it.
Preserve or improve matching performance even if that increases configure or compile complexity.
hard_constraints: Do not introduce runtime fallback from Hyperscan to Vectorscan or from Vectorscan to Hyperscan. Backend choice remains build-time.
Qt regex remains the only runtime fallback.
Do not require SSE2 or SSSE3 on ARM Vectorscan paths.
Do not enable Vectorscan on Windows arm64 in this task.
Preserve explicit user override flags for KLOGG_USE_HYPERSCAN and KLOGG_USE_VECTORSCAN.
If both backends are enabled simultaneously, fail configuration with a clear message.
Avoid unrelated refactors outside the backend-selection path.
implementation_requirements: Replace the current coarse platform default logic with explicit OS plus architecture selection.
Normalize architecture detection across CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR, KLOGG_ARCH, MSVC generator platform, and CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES.
Treat x86_64 aliases consistently, including x86_64, amd64, AMD64, and x64.
Treat arm64 aliases consistently, including arm64, aarch64, and ARM64.
Preserve manual override behavior. Defaults should apply only when the user has not explicitly selected a backend.
Emit clear configure-time messages that print selected OS, arch, backend, and fat-runtime mode.
Preserve portable release behavior where possible. Do not silently over-specialize distributed non-fat builds to the local build host unless that is already intentional and documented.

windows-x64: Use the fastest practical non-fat configuration.
Do not attempt Linux-style fat runtime behavior on Windows.
linux-x64: Enable fat runtime when supported by the selected Hyperscan build.
Favor maximum x86 matching performance, including wider runtime variants when toolchain support exists.
Gracefully disable unavailable high-end variants instead of failing the build for optional optimizations.
linux-arm64: Prefer the strongest Arm configuration the compiler can support, including SVE, SVE2, and SVE2_BITPERM when available.
Gracefully fall back to weaker supported Arm configurations if the strongest options are unavailable.
macos-x64: Optimize for runtime performance without making shipped binaries unnecessarily host-specific.
macos-arm64: Optimize for runtime performance on arm64 while keeping packaging sane.
windows-arm64: Force both accelerated backends off by default.
Leave the code organized so a future Windows arm64 plus Vectorscan task can be added cleanly.

changes: Refactor backend default selection to an explicit OS plus architecture matrix.
Add normalized target detection helpers or booleans.
Validate impossible or conflicting configurations with explicit fatal errors.
Keep manual overrides supported.
Parameterize Hyperscan and Vectorscan package options by selected backend and target platform.
For Linux x64 Hyperscan, enable the widest practical performance-oriented runtime variants when supported by the toolchain.
For Linux arm64 Vectorscan, enable maximum supported fat-runtime and Arm feature coverage with graceful fallback.
For non-Linux targets that use accelerated backends, prefer fast non-fat builds.
Avoid settings that silently produce build-host-only artifacts unless explicitly documented.
Keep single-backend linkage behavior.
Add explicit backend compile definitions if needed for backend-aware runtime checks.
Remove unconditional x86-only SSE2 plus SSSE3 gating for all accelerated backends.
Make runtime validation backend-aware and architecture-aware.
For Hyperscan builds, use hs_valid_platform and any necessary x86-specific checks only where appropriate.
For Vectorscan arm64 builds, do not require x86 SIMD flags.
Preserve Qt fallback when backend validation, database creation, or scratch allocation fails.
Stop making ARM targets look unsupported merely because x86 CPUID logic is absent.
If CPU feature probing is still needed for diagnostics, make it backend-aware and architecture-aware.
Avoid coupling backend enablement to x86-only instruction flags.
Update jobs or options so the implemented backend matrix is visible in CI.
Keep Windows arm64 on Qt-only.
Make backend choice obvious in job naming, configure output, or artifact labeling.
Document the new default backend matrix.
Document where fat runtime is intentionally enabled and where it is intentionally off.
Document that Windows arm64 is Qt-only for now and that Vectorscan there is a future follow-up.

design_rules: No x86 SIMD gate on ARM Vectorscan paths.
Prefer maximum supported fat-runtime coverage over simpler configuration when it materially helps matching performance.
When fat runtime is unavailable on the selected target, choose the fastest portable non-fat configuration rather than the simplest compile.
acceptance_criteria: Linux x64 accelerated builds enable fat-runtime behavior when supported.
Linux arm64 accelerated builds enable fat-runtime behavior when supported.
macOS builds do not attempt unsupported fat-runtime configurations.
ARM64 Vectorscan paths are no longer blocked by SSE2 plus SSSE3 checks.
Explicit backend override flags still work.
Configure output clearly reports selected backend and fat-runtime mode.

configure_checks: Configure a Windows x64 build and confirm Hyperscan is selected by default.
Configure a Linux x64 build and confirm Hyperscan is selected by default.
Configure a Linux arm64 build and confirm Vectorscan is selected by default.
Configure a macOS x64 build and confirm Hyperscan is selected by default.
Configure a macOS arm64 build and confirm Vectorscan is selected by default.
Configure a Windows arm64 build and confirm both accelerated backends are disabled by default.
runtime_checks: Run at least one focused regex smoke test on each accelerated backend path that can be exercised in the available environment.
Confirm Qt fallback still works when the accelerated backend is unavailable or invalid.
Confirm ARM64 accelerated paths do not trip the old x86-only runtime gate.
regression_checks: Ensure no target links both Hyperscan and Vectorscan.
Ensure current Windows x64 behavior is preserved or improved.
Ensure CI still builds intended artifacts and that backend selection is visible in logs.

non_goals: Do not implement Windows arm64 plus Vectorscan in this task.
Do not switch the repo to all-Vectorscan.
Do not change regex semantics or user-visible search behavior beyond backend selection and runtime validation.
final_response_requirements: List exactly which files were changed.
Summarize the final implemented backend matrix.
State where fat runtime is enabled and where it is intentionally disabled.
Call out any optional performance flags that were enabled only when toolchain support existed.
Call out any remaining upstream or toolchain limitations.
End with a short note about the next logical follow-up for Windows arm64 plus Vectorscan.
